insights.title: Rainfall has increased
insights.body: Yearly rain went from about 1640 mm to 1873 mm.

insights.title: Downpours are becoming more common
insights.body: Days with 20 mm or more of rain went from about 26 to 31 a year (first vs last 10 years). Bare soil during these storms washes away fastest.

insights.title: Best-matched crops for this area
insights.body: Rice, Maize and Soybean score highest on climate, water and soil fit.

outlook.method: Theil-Sen trend + Mann-Kendall test on 2001-2024 yearly data, extended to 2035 with an 80% prediction range. Where there is no clear trend, the 2001-2024 average is projected. Statistical extrapolation, not a climate-model forecast.

consequences.headline: More downpours: about 39 heavy-rain days a year by 2035
consequences.detail: Up from about 29 today. Each downpour on bare soil washes away topsoil and the fertiliser in it; fields here are barest in Jan, Feb and Mar.
consequences.action: Keep the ground covered (a legume or crop residue) through the rainy months.

consequences.headline: About 26% more rain by 2035
consequences.detail: Yearly rain trends from about 1,772 mm to 2,236 mm. More water, but also more waterlogging on heavy soil.
consequences.action: Keep drains open; raised beds help crops that hate wet feet.
